method: Full reads of two pinned reference implementations; verified Git blob and SHA256. No parallel hash execution in this audit.
findings: BLAKE2bp uses4 BLAKE2b leaves with128-byte blocks; BLAKE2sp uses8 BLAKE2s leaves with64-byte blocks. Both buffer512-byte stripes and feed full-width leaf digests into a depth-one root. Leaf configured output width is explicitly replaced with inner_length.
Keyed initialization feeds a padded key block to every leaf and clears temporary key block; root and last leaf are marked last_node. These tree domains differ from sequential BLAKE2 digests.

Without OpenMP, explicit for-loops visit all lanes. With OpenMP, each thread handles exactly its thread index in a parallel region requesting4/8 threads; code does not check actual team size or use omp for. Correct coverage relies on obtaining the requested team size, a static concern not runtime-reproduced here.

Finalization checks null/short output before consuming leaf state, but ignores leaf final return values before feeding local hash array to root. Repeated-final invalid lifecycle could therefore read uninitialized local digest values; not executed.

Both update and one-shot paths form lane-offset pointers before checking whether a full stripe remains. Their dereferences are separately guarded; pointer-range portability remains unqualified. Selftest sections depend on absent blake2-kat.h.
limits: No OpenMP team-size, cryptographic oracle or all-platform qualification.
